column1: # WHAT FAMILYSEARCH ACTUALLY HOLDS FOR SOUTH AFRICA — measured 17 September 2026.
# The worklist said eleven record sets. There are THIRTY-TWO. All 3,502 FamilySearch
# collections were enumerated through /service/search/hr/v2/collections and filtered;
# the counts below are the collections' own published figures.
# THE POINT OF THIS FILE IS THE LAST TWO ROWS OF EACH BLOCK. A collection's TITLE gives
# the span of the records. Its INDEX may stop far earlier, and an index that stops is
# indistinguishable, from outside, from a family that leaves no record. Both cliffs
# below were measured by counting exact-year hits, not read off a description.

row 81 cannot be answered here. There is no post-1970 South African marriage indexed in this set, so no register image of that date can be reached by name.
South Africa, Civil Death Registration, 1953-1967 is a NAME INDEX TO 1966

KURT died 1968. HENRY ROBERT died 11 September 1969. LEONARD died 1973 or 1979. ALL THREE FALL AFTER THE LAST YEAR FAMILYSEARCH INDEXES A SOUTH AFRICAN CIVIL DEATH. Their absence from it is a property of the index, not of their lives.
South Africa, Transvaal, Estate Files, 1950-1993 — id 2144007
the collection's own words: "Images of copies of DEATH NOTICES from probate estate files from the historic province of Transvaal ... National Archives of South Africa, Pretoria"
a South African death notice names the deceased's PARENTS. The title spans 1950 to 1993, which brackets Kurt in 1968, Henry Robert in 1969, both of Leonard's candidate years, and Martha Maud in 1986.
SEVEN WAYPOINTS: 1955, 1956, 1957, 1958, 1958-1959, 1959, 1960. Read from /service/cds/recapi/collections/2144007/waypoints.

THE SET IS PUBLISHED FOR 1955 TO 1960 ONLY. Its own page says "This collection is being published as images become available." Nothing in it can touch any death in this family. Worth re-checking whenever FamilySearch adds to it — this is the one instrument that would answer row 96 without Home Affairs.
the Orange Free State equivalent, id 1407787, IS complete — 57 waypoints, 1951 to 2006. So the gap in the Transvaal set is a publishing gap, not a survival gap.
